concept: Estimate using rates and assumed values

card.statement: A rough estimate is constructed by choosing simple assumed rates and values rather than searching for exact measurements.
card.knowledge: A rough estimate can be built from simple assumed rates and values.

title: A rough estimate can be built from simple assumed rates

concept: Estimate using rates and assumed values

card.statement: The estimation procedure multiplies an assumed rate by the relevant time interval or the number of persons involved.
card.knowledge: An assumed rate is combined over a relevant time or number of persons to give an estimate.

title: An assumed rate is combined over a relevant time

concept: Estimate using rates and assumed values

card.statement: An average adult needs about 2000 2500 kilocalories per day, a value used in the rice-family estimation problem.
card.knowledge: An average adult needs about 2000–2500 kilocalories per day.

title: An average adult needs about 2000–2500 kilocalories per day

concept: Estimate using rates and assumed values

card.statement: To estimate rice for a family, one assumes that all their calorie needs come from rice alone.
card.knowledge: In the rice model, all calorie needs are assumed to come from rice alone.

title: In the rice model, all calorie needs are assumed

concept: Estimate using rates and assumed values

card.statement: A rough estimate can be formed by assuming simple rates, for example breaths per minute and volume per breath, then multiplying over the relevant time period.
card.knowledge: Rates such as breaths per minute and volume per breath can be used to estimate totals.

title: Rates such as breaths per minute and volume per breath

card.statement: Because scientific ideas must be communicated clearly and unambiguously, science selects words that have exact meanings instead of informal or variable meanings.
card.knowledge: Scientific ideas must be communicated clearly and unambiguously, so science relies on precise terms.

title: Scientific ideas must be communicated clearly and unambiguously

card.statement: Scientists around the world need a shared set of specific terms so they can describe observations, compare their results, and build a common body of scientific knowledge.
card.knowledge: Scientists worldwide need a shared language of specific terms to describe observations, compare results, and build ideas together.

title: Scientists worldwide need a shared language of specific terms

concept: Symbols arise from history and agreement

card.statement: The symbols used in science are generally based on their historical origins and on agreements made by the scientific community, not simply on convenience or short abbreviations.
card.knowledge: Scientific symbols often arise from historical roots and international agreements rather than from abbreviations of convenience.

title: Scientific symbols often arise from historical roots and international agreements

concept: Symbols arise from history and agreement

card.statement: The speed of light is written as c because the Latin word celeritas, meaning speed, is the root of this symbol.
card.knowledge: The symbol c for the speed of light comes from the Latin word celeritas, meaning speed.

title: The symbol c for the speed of light comes from the Latin word celeritas

concept: Symbols arise from history and agreement

card.statement: One of the defining values in physics is the speed of light, which is set exactly at 299792458 metres per second.
card.knowledge: The speed of light is a physical constant defined to be exactly 299792458 m/s.

title: The speed of light is a physical constant defined to be exactly 299792458 m/s

card.statement: A useful way to test an estimate is to check it using a second, independent calculation or reasoning path.
card.knowledge: An estimate can be checked by a second independent line of reasoning.

card.statement: If independent estimates agree closely, confidence in the original estimate increases.
card.knowledge: When two independent estimates are close, the estimate is more trustworthy.

title: When two independent estimates are close

card.statement: The balloon calculation produced about 8640 litres, which is close to the first estimate of 10,000 litres.
card.knowledge: The balloon calculation gave about 8640 litres, close to the first estimate of 10,000 litres.

title: The balloon calculation gave about 8640 litres

card.statement: The magnifying glass symbolises careful observation — noticing patterns and paying attention to what might otherwise be missed.
Careful observation involves looking closely at natural patterns and details in order to notice what is not immediately apparent.
Scientific exploration depends on careful observation to identify patterns and details in nature.
